vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: yuketang-mcp
Version: 1.0.4

The skill bundle is a legitimate MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for the Yuketang (xuetangx.com) education platform. It provides tools for teachers to manage classes, view student statistics, and track assignments. The setup scripts (setup.sh and setup.js) use the standard 'mcporter' utility to configure the MCP server and include a minor telemetry report (claw_report) to the official backend (open-ai.xuetangx.com) to log installation duration. No evidence of malicious behavior, unauthorized data exfiltration, or prompt injection attacks was found.

llm.summary: The skill generally matches its stated purpose (connecting to a Yuketang MCP service) but has metadata inconsistencies and setup steps that could expose your secret and perform remote telemetry, so proceed with caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to provide Yuketang (雨课堂) teaching-data queries and the code and SKILL.md consistently require a YUKETANG_SECRET and configure an MCP endpoint — that is coherent with the described purpose. However, registry metadata lists no required environment variables while package.json and the SKILL.md/setup scripts clearly require YUKETANG_SECRET, an inconsistency that should have been reflected in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and tools are focused on registering an MCP connector and calling Yuketang MCP endpoints to fetch classroom and student data. The SKILL.md does not instruct reading unrelated system files. It does, however, instruct running setup scripts that call external services and run npx mcporter commands (see 'install_mechanism' and 'environment_proportionality' notes).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-first skill (no formal install spec) but the setup scripts invoke npx mcporter (which will fetch code from npm if not present). Using npx is common but means remote packages will be downloaded at setup time — moderate risk compared with instruction-only skills with no network installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only one secret (YUKETANG_SECRET) is required and that is appropriate for authenticating to the Yuketang MCP service. But the setup commands pass the secret on the npx command line and write MCP config entries (project config) that may contain the Authorization header; this can expose the secret via shell history, process arguments, or in the written config file. The skill also performs a silent telemetry call (mcporter call yuketang-mcp claw_report) during setup which transmits installation timing metadata to the MCP service.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' or system-wide privileges. Setup attempts to add a project-scoped MCP server entry (or instructs you to add a config file), which is normal for an MCP connector. It does not modify other skills' configs beyond writing/asking you to write an MCP config file in common project locations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Key things to consider before installing: (1) The skill requires YUKETANG_SECRET even though the registry metadata omitted it — expect to provide this secret. (2) The setup scripts call 'npx mcporter' and may place your Authorization value into a project MCP config; running the npx command with the secret on the command line can expose it to shell history and process lists. Prefer setting the environment variable (not passing the secret inline), inspect the created config file (e.g., .mcp/config.json or .cursor/mcp.json) to see whether the secret was written in plaintext, and rotate the secret if you suspect exposure. (3) The setup performs a telemetry call to the MCP server; verify you trust the MCP endpoint domain (open-ai.xuetangx.com) and the Yuketang secret issuer (yuketang.cn) before proceeding. (4) If you cannot verify the publisher or domains, consider manually adding the MCP configuration (copy the config snippet printed by the script) instead of running the provided scripts, and avoid running commands that embed the secret directly on the command line.
